To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hCaN pulse sequence can be used to record direct 15N-detector experiments within a few hours.

we present a new 15N-detecting NMR experiment, which allows to record 2D N15N spectra on proteins within a short time, and which can be used to study proteins at conditions where 1H-detected experiments are not applicable.

a new 2D 1H,15N experiment, hCaN, is presented that allows direct detection of 15N nuclei in biomolecules and that this method is demonstrated on a small globular protein and on two larger, more flexible proteins, including a protein fragment containing many SerPro repeats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of NMR experiments to detect 15N nuclei directly.
the development of NMR experiments to detect low-γ nuclei.
the development of novel NMR methods for studying proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hCaN 15N experiments are very useful for the study of proteins with fast amide proton exchange and for the study of unstructured proteins.
the hCaN 15N-detector experiment allows for the acquisition of 2D 13C, 15N correlation spectra of proteins with a molecular weight up to 30 kDa in 2–3 h.
the new hCaN experiments are very powerful and useful for a variety of proteins and peptides, especially those that exchange rapidly and/or are difficult to dissolve in D2O.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hCaN experiments are useful for proteins that have a relatively slow 15N relaxation rate (R1), such as proteins with a high content of prolines, or proteins that are in a state of rapid exchange of amide protons.
the hCaN 15N-detector experiment allows for the acquisition of 2D 1H-13C and 1H-15N spectra of small to medium-sized proteins in a few hours, and for larger systems in a few days.
the hCaN 15N-detector experiment is a valuable tool for the study of protein structure and dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
15N direct detection can be used to record 2D 1H–15N correlation experiments on a time scale comparable to that of 2D 13C-detected experiments.
the hCaN 15N experiment is a valuable tool for the structural and functional analysis of biomolecules, especially when the sample is limited, or if the sample is unstable at high concentrations.
1H is an excellent polarization transfer vehicle for low-γ nuclei and that the polarization of the 1N spin is a valuable resource for NMR spectroscopists.
